Error.description: A refusal: one code of `x-insula-errors` with its fixed sentence. By status: 400: `access_pass_invalid`, `id_too_short`, `invalid_request`, `invalid_slug`, `setting_invalid`, `setting_unsupported`; 401: `audience_mismatch`, `token_expired`, `unauthenticated`; 403: `forbidden`; 404: `app_not_found`, `frame_unavailable`, `not_found`, `ref_not_found`, `release_not_found`; 409: `app_deleting`, `repository_name_taken`, `slug_held`, `slug_reserved`, `slug_taken`; 429: `rate_limited`; 500: `internal_error`; 502: `repository_create_failed`; 503: `authorizer_unavailable`, `repository_unavailable`, `slug_generation_failed`. On every route, a token that does not verify answers one of the 401 codes, with `details.reason` naming why on `unauthenticated`, and an authorizer that gave no answer is `authorizer_unavailable`, in which case nothing is written. A path or a method under the API root that this document does not describe answers 404 `not_found`.

info.description: An app is a git repository and an address. Creating an app creates its repository; a push to a branch builds a preview, and a pushed tag that starts with `v` releases that commit to the app's address. This API creates, reads, changes and deletes apps and reads their deploys, build logs and releases. Deploying is a push to the repository and has no route here. Every route verifies a bearer token and asks the installation's authorizer one question before any effect. Every refusal is one envelope with a code of the table in `x-insula-errors`.

get.description:
The edge's check of a request on a private address: whether it may
pass the gate, and for how many seconds the edge may keep that answer.
The caller is the edge, with the bearer of the installation's internal
routes. It is not under the API root: under a base path it stays at
`/internal`.

With `session`, the request carried the address's access cookie: the
gate session it names is loaded, and the authorizer is asked
`gate.access` of the app as the person signed in, with their subject,
their organizations and the email address the identity provider
verified at sign-in. A session that is gone answers the reason
`session`; a deny answers the authorizer's reason.

A session a password opened names no person. It admits on the one app
it was opened for and answers the reason `password_session` on any
other, without a question. On its own app the authorizer is asked
`gate.access` as the installation's own client, with `via`
`password_session` and the `password_version` the visitor was let in
with; a password replaced or removed since answers `password_changed`.

Without it, the request carried `X-Insula-Capture-Pass`: the pass is
verified for `host`; then the authorizer is asked `gate.access` of the
app as the installation's own client, with `via` `capture` in the
resource. A pass that does not verify, an app or host that does not
match, and a deny are each answered `admit` false with a reason, which
the edge treats as a request without a pass.

Refusals:

- `unauthenticated` (401): the bearer is not the internal one.
- `authorizer_unavailable` (503): the authorizer gave no answer.

parameters.description: The app's id, from the edge's route of the host.
parameters.name: project

parameters.description: The host the request was addressed to.
parameters.name: host

parameters.name: session

reason.description: Why the request was refused: `session`, `app_not_found`, `host_mismatch` or the authorizer's reason for a session; `pass_unavailable`, `pass_invalid`, `app_not_found`, `host_mismatch` or `access_refused` for a capture pass.

ttl.description: Seconds the edge may keep an admission; 0 with a refusal.

200.description: Whether the request may pass, and for how long the answer holds.

post.description:
The gate's request for a one-time pass to a private app's host, made
once the visitor is signed in at the gate. The caller is the edge,
with the bearer of the installation's internal routes. It is not under
the API root: under a base path it stays at `/internal`.

The gate session is loaded and the authorizer is asked `gate.access`
of the app as the access check asks it. On an allow, a pass is written
for `host` and answered: good once, for that host, for 60 seconds. On
a deny no pass is written, and the answer carries the reason and the
address the visitor is signed in with, which the gate's page shows. A
session that is gone answers the reason `session`, and the gate signs
the visitor in again.

Refusals:

- `unauthenticated` (401): the bearer is not the internal one.
- `authorizer_unavailable` (503): the authorizer gave no answer.

session.description: The gate session, 32 bytes in hex.

pass.description: The pass, on an allow. Sent once, in the query of one redirect to the host.

reason.description: On a refusal, `session`, `app_not_found`, `host_mismatch`, or the authorizer's reason.

post.description:
The edge's redemption of a pass on the host it arrived at, before the
edge sets the host's access cookie. The caller is the edge, with the
bearer of the installation's internal routes. It is not under the API
root: under a base path it stays at `/internal`.

The pass's MAC is verified for `host` as the `kind` the edge names
and its expiry read; then its row is deleted, which is its one use.
The answer names the gate session and when it ends, which the cookie
lives no longer than. `kind` is the path the pass arrived on: `access`
for `/.latere/access`, and `frame` for `/.latere/frame`, where the
edge sets the cookie a frame of another site carries. A pass of one
kind is refused as the other with the reason `mac`, and keeps its one
use.

Refusals:

- `unauthenticated` (401): the bearer is not the internal one.
- `access_pass_invalid` (400): the pass is not good for this host now. `details.reason` is `malformed`, `mac`, `host`, `expired` or `used`, and `details.host` names the host.
- `invalid_request` (400): `kind` is neither `access` nor `frame`. `details.field` is `kind`.

kind.description: What the pass is redeemed as, the kind of the path it arrived on.

session.description: The gate session, 32 bytes in hex.

post.description:
The gate's question whether a password opens a private app, asked
when a visitor types one on the gate's page. The caller is the edge,
with the bearer of the installation's internal routes. It is not under
the API root: under a base path it stays at `/internal`.

The edge sends a proof of what the visitor typed and never the
password. The authorizer, which keeps the password, is asked
`gate.access` of the app as the installation's own client, with `via`
`password` and the proof. On an allow a session is written for the
visit, bound to this app and to the version of the password it was let
in with, naming no person, for 24 hours, and a pass is written for
`host` and answered: good once, for that host, for 60 seconds, and
redeemed as any access pass. A browser that names the visit it
already holds as `session` is answered with a pass for that visit and
no new one. An app holds at most 5,000 live visits, and the one that
opens past that ends the oldest. On a deny nothing is written and the
answer carries the reason: `no_password`, `password_required` or
`password_wrong`, or another reason of the authorizer's.

An empty `proof` opens nothing. It asks only whether the app has a
password, which the deny `password_required` says, and is how the gate
learns to show its password page. The app's name is answered with
`password_required` and `password_wrong` alone, since that page shows
it.

Refusals:

- `unauthenticated` (401): the bearer is not the internal one.
- `invalid_request` (400): `proof` is neither empty nor 43 characters of base64url. `details.field` is `proof`, and the value is in no answer.
- `authorizer_unavailable` (503): the authorizer gave no answer, or allowed a question that carried no proof, or allowed without naming the password's version.

proof.description: SHA-256 over `latere-app-password/v1`, a zero byte, the app's id in lower case, a zero byte and the password, in base64url with no padding; or empty, to ask whether the app has a password.

session.description: The visit the visitor's browser already holds for this app, 32 bytes in hex, when the gate's cookie names one. A right password is answered with a pass for that visit while it is live, this app's and of the password's current version, and no second one is opened.

name.description: The app's name, on an allow and with `password_required` and `password_wrong`.

pass.description: The pass, on an allow. Sent once, in the query of one redirect to the host.

reason.description: On a refusal, `no_password`, `password_required`, `password_wrong`, `app_not_found`, `host_mismatch`, or another reason of the authorizer's.

session.description: On an allow, the session of the visit, 32 bytes in hex, which the gate names in its own cookie so that a sign-out there ends it.

The session one sign-in at the gate creates, for 24 hours. The caller
is the edge, after it verified the identity provider's ID token and
listed the visitor's organizations once. `email` is the address the

session of `sub` is deleted with its passes, and every host's access
cookie bound to them is refused at its next uncached check. The edge

the issuer's keys before it calls this route. The caller is the edge,
with the bearer of the installation's internal routes. It is not under
the API root: under a base path it stays at `/internal`.

- `unauthenticated` (401): the bearer is not the internal one.
- `invalid_request` (400): `sub` is missing. `details.reason` is `sub`.

host's access cookie and frame cookie bound to one is refused at its
next uncached check. A session that is already gone answers the same

with its passes. The caller is the edge, with the bearer of the
installation's internal routes. It is not under the API root: under a
base path it stays at `/internal`.

Refusals:

- `unauthenticated` (401): the bearer is not the internal one.

post.description:
The sink the platform delivers the events of the app repositories to. It
answers 200 with what the delivery did: `processed`, `duplicate` or
`ignored`.

The caller is the platform's service account, and the route is served only
by an installation that reads the app repositories. It is not under the API
root: under a base path it stays at `/internal`.

The delivery's id is `Origo-Delivery`, or the body's `id` without the
header, and its kind is `Origo-Event`, or the body's `kind`. The id of a
push is recorded with what the delivery creates, so a second delivery of
one push creates nothing and is answered `duplicate`.

A `renamed` or `transferred` delivery moves the app's push and SSH
addresses to the owner name its repository has now, read from the
repository rather than from the event, and is answered `processed`. Its id
is not recorded, so a second delivery reads the name again. One whose
repository was deleted is answered `ignored`.

A delivery of any other kind, whose `repo` names no app, or a push whose
app is deleted is answered `ignored`.

For a push, every update of a branch becomes a preview deploy, after
`deploy.create` is asked for the pusher, and every update of a tag that
starts with `v` becomes a release, after `app.release` is asked for the
pusher. A denied preview creates nothing, and a denied release is recorded
as `refused`. An update that deletes its reference is skipped.

Refusals:

- `invalid_request` (400): the body is not JSON or is larger than 1 MiB. `details.reason` is `body`.
- `invalid_request` (400): the delivery id is missing or longer than 128 characters. `details.reason` is `delivery`.

Ends every sign-in the caller has at private apps: the ones a frame
pass made for a page that frames their apps, and the ones they made
themselves at the gate's sign-in, on every browser. The back end of
a page a person is signed in to calls it with the person's token
when they sign out of that page, before it drops the token. Nothing
else tells this API of that sign-out: a person who only ever saw
their private apps in such a page never signed in at the gate, so
the identity provider sends the gate no logout for them.

Every app host's cookie bound to an ended session is refused at its
next check, within 60 seconds by default and at most 600, the time
the edge keeps an allow. A frame pass not yet used ends with its
session. The cookie itself stays in the browser until it expires
and admits nothing.

The route names no app. The question is `gate.access` on the
account the token acts in, asked of the installation's authorizer
with the caller's token as it is: a person's token is allowed in
their own account and an organization member's in the
organization's. The sessions ended are those of the token's own
subject, in every account, and nobody else's.

The answer is 204 with no body whether or not a session existed.

Refusals:

- `forbidden` (403): the authorizer refuses the caller `gate.access` on the account. `details.reason` carries its reason: `session_read_only` for a hosted agent's session token, which ends none of the sessions of the person it acts for, and `grant` for a key whose grants do not name `gate.access` for every app.
- `rate_limited` (429): the caller ended their sessions 30 times within a minute. `details.limit` and `details.window_seconds` name the limit. A call the authorizer refused is not counted, so a refused key of the same person does not use the limit up.
- `authorizer_unavailable` (503): the authorizer gave no answer, and nothing was ended. Call again.

becomes `deleting` and its addresses stop serving it.

The deletion then finishes on its own: the deploys still under way are
canceled, the files of every deploy are removed, and the repository is
deleted. Until then the app is still read and listed, as `deleting`, and
still holds its slug.

Once it has finished, the app answers `app_not_found` and its slug is held
for this account for seven days, during which a create on that slug restores
the app.

Deleting an app that is already `deleting` answers the same 202.

- `forbidden` (403): the authorizer denied `app.delete`. `details.action` names the action, and `details.reason` the authorizer's reason when it gave one.

so a client that keeps an app's id finds the app after its owner

current slug from the answer. The answer is the same document either
way.

with that id. No create or rename takes a slug of that form. An app
that had one before keeps it and is found by it too, unless an app of
this account has that value as its id, which is then the app found.

Without a bearer it answers only an app anyone with its address may
open, public or unlisted and published, among every account's apps,
and only its id, slug, name and address (`OpenApp`). A copy that kept
an app's id, such as a shared conversation's, reads the app's current
address by it after a rename. Reads without a bearer are limited to
120 a minute from one address, counted with those of an app's
pictures, and no cache keeps the answer.

- `app_not_found` (404): the slug or id names no app, an app of another account, a deleted app, or an app the caller may not read; without a bearer, also an app that is private or unpublished. and answers the app as changed.

repository's `push_url` changes with it while `clone_url` stays, and the old
slug is held for this account for seven days. A new slug passes the same
rules as a slug given to a create.

already: an app becomes `public` when its listing in the gallery is
approved, and only then. `unlisted` opens the app to anyone who has its
address, and `private` to its owner, an organization's members and the
people it is shared with.

`state` takes `paused` to unpublish an active app and `active` to publish

publishing again serves the same release at once. An app the platform
paused stays paused.

`settings` is merged into the stored settings key by key.

the account or organization the token acts in, and `app.read` decides,
so the owner reads the screenshot of a private or unpublished app.

and the screenshot is answered only while the address the deploy serves
is `public` or `unlisted` and the app is published, the way the
address itself is served. Reads without a bearer are limited to 120 a
minute from one address.

without one, `public, max-age=3600`, so an address made private stops
being served from a shared cache within the hour. The `ETag` names

- `unauthenticated` (401): a bearer was sent and failed verification. It is never read as no credential.

post.description:
Hands the caller the address to point a frame at, so that a page on
another site shows a private app to the person signed in to that page
without a second sign-in. A private app's own sign-in is a page of
the gate, which no frame of another site can show, so a frame of a
private app's address shows a page that offers the app in a new tab.
Call this route with the address of the app the frame is about to
show, and use the `url` of the answer as the frame's address. The
pass in it is redeemed only by a frame that a page of another site
than the app's draws: opened in a tab, or drawn by a page under the
apps domain, `url` answers 400 and the pass stays unused.

`url` is on the same host as `address` and carries a pass good once,
for that host, until `expires_at`, 60 seconds after the call. The
app's host exchanges it for a cookie only a frame carries, good for
one hour, and then shows the path, the query and the fragment of
`address`. Ask again each time the frame is drawn, on every mount and
reload: a pass is used by the first load, each pass is an hour of its
own, and a second load of the same `url` shows the app only while the
cookie of the first is still there.

The pass is the caller's own: the question is `gate.access`, asked of
the installation's authorizer with the caller's token as it is. A
person's token is allowed for an app of their own account, and an
organization member's for the organization's app. A hosted agent's
session token is refused, and so is a key whose grants do not name
`gate.access`.

A frame that cannot show the app shows a page that offers it in a
new tab, and that page posts one message to the page that frames it,
`{"type": "latere:frame", "state": "expired"}` or
`{"type": "latere:frame", "state": "refused"}`. Listen for it and act
on the state.

`expired` means no sign-in admits the frame: the hour ended, the
person signed out or lost access, or the pass was used or older than
60 seconds. Call this route again and point the frame at the new
`url`, once; if that frame posts a message too, fall back.

`refused` means the pass was redeemed and the browser sent no cookie
back: it keeps none for a frame of another site, and a new pass ends
the same way. Fall back to what the page shows without a frame.

The installation names the origins whose pages may frame a private
app. A page of any other origin is refused by the browser when it
draws the frame, whatever pass it holds.

When the person signs out of the page, end what the passes made
with `DELETE /v1/apps/gate/sessions`.

Refusals:

- `frame_unavailable` (404): this installation names no origin that may frame a private app, so no frame pass is handed out.
- `app_not_found` (404): the slug or id names no app, an app of another account, or an app the caller may not read. `details.slug` names the slug or the id the path gave.
- `invalid_request` (400): `address` is not an `https` address on one of this app's hosts: `<slug>`, `next--<slug>`, or the host of one of its deploys that has a preview. `details.field` is `address`, and `details.reason` is `length`, `parse`, `scheme`, `host` or `path`. An address that is no `https` address at all is refused before the app is looked at, whatever the slug; one on a host that is not the app's is refused only to a caller the authorizer allowed, so a caller who may not read the app gets `app_not_found` for every address.
- `forbidden` (403): the authorizer refuses the caller `gate.access` on an app the caller may read. `details.reason` carries its reason, such as `session_read_only` for a hosted agent's token and `grant` for a key.
- `rate_limited` (429): the caller made 20 calls the authorizer allowed for this app within a minute. `details.limit` and `details.window_seconds` name the limit. A call the authorizer refused is not counted.

get.description:
Answers the build log of one deploy by its full id, without the slug of its
app, when the app is the caller's to read. Each deploy names this route in
its `logs_url`.

The two forms, the parameters and the refusals are those of the route under
the app. The one difference is that this route takes the full id and no
prefix.

Without `text/event-stream` in `Accept`, the answer is the stored log as
`application/x-ndjson`: one JSON object per line, the lines of every
component merged in the order of their time. It is what has been stored so
far and it ends there, whether or not the deploy is still building.

With `text/event-stream` in `Accept`, the answer is a stream of server-sent
events: one event per line, a `: heartbeat` comment every 15 seconds of
silence, and a last event named `end`.

With `follow=1` the stream stays open while the deploy waits or builds and
ends when it leaves building. Without it, the stream sends the stored lines
and ends with the deploy's status as it is at that moment.

Refusals:

- `not_found` (404): the id is not a UUID, names no deploy, names a deploy of another account, or names a deploy of an app the caller may not read. `details.deploy_id` names the id. The answers are the same, so the route tells a caller nothing of an app it may not read.
- `not_found` (404): `component` names a component the deploy does not have. `details.component` names it.
- `invalid_request` (400): `since` is not an integer of at least 0. `details.field` is `since`.
